title: Orecast
body: We are investigating Tok River, Alaska. Orecast brings geological evidence, recorded simulated reactions and the time available to exit an assumed mineral option into one decision that we can inspect. Financial outputs remain hypothetical.
sources: Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Terrain: Mapzen Terrarium (AWS Open Data).

title: Time and evidence
body: The decision has three distinct clocks: evidence collected and published in 2016, five simulated days, and assumed 30-, 90- or 180-day sale horizons. We now use a whole-lot entry of 30,050 dollars, including an assumed 50-dollar fee. The 30,000-dollar reference comes from two selected historical signing payments. It is not a current quote or the full cost of either historical agreement.
preparation: Fund size is exactly $1,502,500. Per-option risk is $30,050. Open risk and lifetime cohort commitments are each capped at $150,250, with no more than five positions. Historical Tibbs and Northway obligations are not included in the two signing-payment statistic; fees and the no-additional-obligations demo setting remain assumptions. A/B evidence partitions are not legal parcels or fractional traded units.

title: Observed evidence
body: We begin with 67 measured sediment samples from Tok River, Alaska: 33 in Area A and 34 in B. Source provenance stays attached to each observation. Under the proposed gold-assay screen, A passes and B fails. The samples provide observed evidence, not recoverable ounces or geological success probabilities. Those remain separate assumptions. Map claims and illustrative squares provide context; they do not establish available mineral rights or an investment.
sources: Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Terrain: Mapzen Terrarium (AWS Open Data).
preparation: Technical Q&A: at the proposed 0.01 ppm primary Au screen, A has 25 of 33 passing and B has 16 of 34. The rule requires at least ten classified observations and a qualifying lower bound of 50%. Preserve primary assay qualifiers and retests separately.

title: Gold forecast and assignment
body: Read the layers from top to bottom. Observed assays screen eligibility. Recorded simulated support is compared with the matching Claude sports-placebo reference. Orecast changes the assumed gold price first, then recomputes gross material value, success-state interest value, option assignment proceeds, and dated sale/no-sale cash and return. Recoverable ounces, ownership, conversion, geological success, buyer consideration, fees and sale hazard are separate assumptions. At each possible sale date the assignment payoff is geological success times the positive part of success-state interest value less buyer consideration. The 7% coefficient is an uncalibrated gold response cap. It is neither a direct assignment markup nor an investment-loss limit. The response is retained across sale dates without monthly compounding. Strict research readiness remains failed; the financial path is explicitly hypothetical. Whole-lot entry, fees and commitment limits are checked separately. The independent baseline valuation stays at 1500 dollars rather than being scaled to create profit. No trade execution occurs.
sources: Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Terrain: Mapzen Terrarium (AWS Open Data).

title: Recorded scenario contrast
body: The recorded support comparison is unchanged. Mine approval gives minus 0.0252 support and assumed gold of 1996.47 dollars an ounce; court blockage gives plus 0.0307 and 2004.30 dollars. With the same 30,050-dollar lot, expected 90-day cash is minus 29,344.55 dollars for approval and minus 29,339.78 for blockage. Expected option returns are minus 97.65% and minus 97.64%. Both are skips. The gold-first valuation remains independent of the entry premium. The matching sports-placebo reference covers days three through five; it is not an untreated control. The 7% response is an uncalibrated gold coefficient, not a loss limit. Research checks still fail. We did not raise the exit valuation to manufacture a margin.
sources: Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Terrain: Mapzen Terrarium (AWS Open Data).

title: Time and return
body: At 30,050 dollars upfront, the unchanged zero-growth baseline assignment value is only 1500 dollars. At 90 days, expected cash is minus 29,342.40 dollars and expected option return is minus 97.65%. The result is skip. Thirty and 180 days also fail: more opportunities to sell cannot rescue this price mismatch. A 25% expected 90-day return would require 77,022.34 dollars of gross assignment proceeds, held constant across possible sale dates. That is a required underwriting hurdle, not a forecast or an observed resale quote. It does not replace the independent 1500-dollar model valuation. Sale probability remains an assumed 48.8%, with 51.2% no sale. Unsold marks stay separate from cash.
preparation: The cash chart uses the full zero-to-minus-$32,000 axis. Baseline 30/90/180-day cash is −$29,760.00/−$29,342.40/−$28,980.11. Non-annualized return divides cash by all $30,050 upfront. No-sale cash is −$30,050; even a completed sale has −$28,600 net cash. The 180-day horizon plus 15-day closing buffer fits inside the assumed 365-day maturity.

title: Demonstration
body: On /swarm, compare approval with blockage for Area A at 90 days. The gold forecast changes, but both whole-lot scenarios remain skips. Approval has minus 29,344.55 dollars expected cash; blockage has minus 29,339.78. The 25% resale hurdle is not a forecast. Next, validate real contract costs, assignment liquidity and paired prospective outcomes. The historical pilot did not establish an edge.
sources: Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Terrain: Mapzen Terrarium (AWS Open Data).
preparation: Allow up to twenty seconds for the live comparison within this 45-second slide. Use the refreshed recorded /swarm path, Area A, 90 days, simulated day 5. The separate Decision workbench startup/reset uses a different synthetic preset and must not be conflated with this comparison. If switching is slow, point to the saved capture.

title: Baseline cash calculation
body: The unchanged baseline assignment proceeds are 1500 dollars. Subtract a 50-dollar exit fee and 30,050-dollar upfront commitment: the sale branch has minus 28,600 dollars cash. No sale has minus 30,050. Weighting the branches by 48.8% and 51.2% gives minus 13,956.80 and minus 15,385.60, summing to minus 29,342.40. Dividing by 30,050 gives minus 97.64526%, not annualized. To require a 25% expected return with the same sale probability, solve S equals 30,050 times 1.25 divided by 0.488 plus 50, giving 77,022.34 dollars. This is a constant gross assignment-proceeds hurdle at every possible sale date, not a forecast. We keep 500 assumed recoverable ounces, 2000-dollar gold, 50% ownership, 2% conversion, 25% geological success and 4000-dollar buyer consideration unchanged. Those assumptions still produce 1500 dollars. The independent valuation does not justify the new entry premium, so the model skips.

title: Historical pilot
body: This is a small retrospective equity component test, separate from the Tok option calculation. It uses twelve source-selected 2020–2025 permitting or court events, nine Pebble/Northern Dynasty and three Donlin/NOVAGOLD. Five observations are held out for each horizon, but the five- and twenty-session cohorts differ. Mean absolute error is measured in percentage points; lower is better. No change gives 2.5562 and 5.9474; gold-only gives 3.1291 and 7.5670; gold plus event gives 8.0596 and 14.3108. The event adjustment did not beat the gold baseline, and no change performs best in both selected cohorts. There are no paired historical swarm outcomes. Limitations include repeated issuers, a source-selected incomplete sample, date-only awareness uncertainty, current-vintage adjusted prices, correlated or anticipated events and vendor precision. GLD is an ETF proxy, not spot gold. This pilot does not validate Tok option returns, the assumed support-to-gold response or incremental swarm value. Next validate paired prospective outcomes and assignment liquidity.
